originality.rationale: The full-q, all-n factor-frequency-level multiplicity formula was not covered by the compared primary or indexed literature. Bell et al. gives level bounds, Bognini–Ammar describes kernel-gap factorizations, the dyadic primary indexed theorem enumerates unweighted factors only, and Balková treats generalized Thue–Morse. Exact object, parameters, and implications were compared. Unindexed equivalent formulas remain a residual risk. An existing all-length unweighted factor-count law was also checked and does not enumerate weighted cylinders.
residual_risks: A pre-2026 or unindexed specialized factor-frequency formula for the valuation-modulo-q word might already imply the theorem; broad search coverage cannot rule this out.
The comparison of the Balková paper is restricted to its abstract and substitution and does not purport to certify every lemma of that full document.

The final three semantic published-finding corpus queries returned the same dyadic factor census and adjacent invariants, with no matching all-length occurrence-frequency table; database recall is not exhaustive.

value.rationale: Complete cylinder-measure multiplicities constitute a motivated exact invariant for automatic words, substantially finer than the known factor-complexity function or a generic upper bound on frequency levels. The all-length three-regime law and sharp binary equal-frequency classification enable exact probabilities of random factors and collision statistics at arbitrary scales.
